title: A Dual-Acting Nitric Oxide Donor and Phosphodiesterase 5 Inhibitor Activates Autophagy in Primary Skin Fibroblasts
projectDescription: In the project “A Dual-Acting Nitric Oxide Donor and Phosphodiesterase 5 Inhibitor Activates Autophagy in Primary Skin Fibroblasts» by Esther Martínez-Martínez and Joern Dengjel, we performed expression proteomics analyzing the response of normal human fibroblasts (NHF) isolated from healthy skin to the drug TOP-N53.
sampleProcessingProtocol: NHF were cultured in 10 cm2 plates and let them grow until they reached ~70% confluence. NHF were serum starved (0.25% FBS) prior to the treatment with vehicle (0.1% DMSO) or TOP-N53 0.1 M for 24 h. Cells were lysed with 1% Na-deoxycholate prepared in 50mM ABC buffer (50mM Ammonium bicarbonate, pH7.5). 1 M of benzonase was added to the cell lysates to digest nucleic acids. Protein concentration was determined by pierce BCA protein assay kit and samples containing 75 g protein were prepared. Samples were reduced with 1 mM DTT and alkylated with 5.5 mM iodoacetamide (Sigma-Aldrich) and they were digested with trypsin HPLC-grade (Promega AG, Dübendorf, Switzerland) overnight. Next, Na-deoxycholate was precipitated with 1% v/v of formic acid and eliminated by 10 min centrifugation at 13000 rpm. The resulting peptide solutions (supernatants) were desalted on C18-based STAGE tips as previously described and analyzed by liquid chromatography-MS/MS
dataProcessingProtocol: Peak detection and relative quantification of peptides and proteins was conducted by MaxQuant version 1.6.2.10. Peaks were searched against a full-length human Uniprot database from March 2016. Enzyme specificity was assigned to trypsin/P and quantitation was based on Label Free Quantification (LFQ). Carbamidomethylcysteine was set as fixed modification, and protein amino-terminal acetylation and oxidation of methionine were set as variable modifications. The MS/MS tolerance was set to 20 ppm. A maximum of three missed cleavages was allowed. Proteins were identified with a minimum of one unique peptide. For protein quantification, a ratio count of two was set. Identification and quantification of peptides and proteins was based on a reverse-database with a false discovery rate (FDR) of 0.01. Peptide length had to be at least 7 amino acids. Identified peptides were re-quantified. For enhanced identification, runs were matched with a match time window of 1 min.
